title: Insert the Missing Character
shortDescription: Find the missing number or letter in rows, columns, grids, triangles and circles.
genZNote: Every puzzle grid has a secret rule. Check rows, then columns, then diagonals — the rule usually shows up in the first two.

sections.heading: Common Rules
bullets: Squares or cubes of numbers; difference of squares.
Middle number = sum/difference/product of outer numbers.
Circle/triangle puzzles: sum of three outer numbers = centre, or sum of opposite numbers constant.
Letter puzzles: convert letters to positions (A = 1 … Z = 26) and apply arithmetic.
Alternating rules: odd and even positions follow different patterns.

steps.name: Test the same rule on another line

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Grid rows (2, 3, 6), (4, 5, 20), (3, 4, ?): rule product of first two → 12. Triangle with outer numbers 5, 6, 7 and centre 18 → sum. Letters: A, C, F, J, ? → gaps +2, +3, +4, so next is O (15).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Missing character problems hide an arithmetic or positional rule common to rows, columns or figures.

highYieldFacts: A rule must hold for every complete line.
commonTraps: Do not apply a rule validated only once.
mustRemember: Test the rule on a second line.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)

questions.prompt: Triangle outer numbers 4, 6, 8 give centre 18. For 5, 7, 9 centre = ?
